content.text:
I've submitted index 14 (Sb 0.236, Y 0.764) as the best composition, but no measurement found real photoactivity. All three readings are at noise level, about ±2×10⁻⁴ % EQE, so index 14 wins only by having the one positive value.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 28 (Sb-rich end) | 0.666 | −1.7×10⁻⁴ |
| 22 (middle) | 0.484 | −2.1×10⁻⁴ |
| 14 (Y-rich side) | 0.236 | +8.3×10⁻⁴ → **+8.3×10⁻⁵** |

This is what the band gaps predict. The known Sb–Y oxide phases have estimated gaps of about 2.7–3.6 eV, too wide to absorb the 2.1 eV illumination. The band-gap model predicted near-zero gaps for the two phases at a 1:1 Sb:Y ratio. That would have put absorption in the middle of the line, so I spent the last measurement on index 22 to test it. It came back at noise level, so those predictions look wrong.

I used all 3 merit measurements. I took no XRD measurements, so which phases are actually in the films is unconfirmed. With readings this close to zero, any of the 26 unmeasured compositions could score as well as index 14, but nothing here points to one that would do clearly better.
